{"reconstruction": "CONTEXT. The sheet is a list of corrections and supplementary calculations for Riemann's Paris prize essay of 1861 ('Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae'). The prize question asked: in a homogeneous infinite body, which temperature states keep a given system of isothermal curves isothermal for all time? The headings 'p. 8', 'p. 12', 'p. 13' refer to pages of that essay. One sentence is in an editor's voice: 'In sequentibus calculos ad confirmandas has propositiones necessarios, e quibus quae supersunt quoad facere potuimus, in integrum restituere conati sumus' ('In what follows we have tried, as far as we could, to restore in full the calculations needed to confirm these propositions from what survives'). The German 'in der Linie' points the same way. So the sheet is most likely an editorial reconstruction sheet (Weber/Dedekind) for the Werke edition of 1876, not a primary Riemann text. The previous page treats related cases (spherical isothermal surfaces); the next page continues the case analysis below.

(A) Correction to p. 8. The heat equation Δu = ∂u/∂t is written in the form (a): Σ_ν p_ν(α) ∂q_ν(β,t)/∂t = Σ T(α,β) Q(β,t), which I read as arising from an ansatz u = Σ_ν p_ν q_ν (my reading). The μ particular solutions p_ν are assumed to satisfy no identity Σ g_ν p_ν = 0.
- Hence there are points α_1,…,α_μ with det[p_ν(α_i)] ≠ 0. This is the standard lemma: functions are linearly independent iff some evaluation matrix at μ points is nonsingular
